newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JULY 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JULY 15.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - According to Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus, the state will financially support reconstruction for housing and troubled businesses in flooded areas.

- A leading northern Moravian metal and mining company, OKD, is finding itself in a tough situation due to blocked railway connections, and it will not be able to continue manufacturing for longer than one week.
- The crown weakened again against the mark during trading yesterday to as low as 19.90. It reached another historic minimum against the dollar -- 34.2.

- American Secretary of State Madeleine Albright welcomed the Czech Republic to NATO yesterday. She met with President Vaclav Havel and other leading politicians at Prague Castle. She said the main task for the Czech Republic is to spend two percent of its GDP on defence by the year 2000.
- Through the Industry and Trade Ministry, Konsolidacni Banka will present a proposal to the cabinet next week to sell 34 percent of tractor maker Zetor to Motokov International.

- Komercni Banka announced that participating sides agreed on conditions for a government guarantee from Ukraine for a credit line for KB of $60 million to support exports of Czech industrial companies.
- Preliminary estimates of damages in agriculture caused by the floods are between 10 and 12 billion crowns, the agrarian chamber said.
MLADA FRONTA DNES - Although water levels are falling in most of the east, water continued to move south yesterday and areas around the Kyjovka River were flooded.
- According to the latest proposal from Health Minister Jan Strasky, which the cabinet should discuss today, patients would pay from five to 10 percent of the cost of their health care each year.
- From today, Konsolidacni Banka will increase its interest rates for timed accounts of up to 10 million crowns by between 1.20 and 3.30 percent to between 10.80 and 13 percent.
- During the first half of this year, Skoda Mlada Boleslav sold a record 161,886 vehicles, a year-on-year increase of 27.2 percent.
- Ceska Rafinerska will decrease its prices for all kinds of petrol by 70 crowns per tonne and motor oil by 100 crowns per tonne.

- The Agriculture Ministry does not see a reason for grocery stores to increase prices due to flooded fields and sties. Deputy Agriculture Minister Antonin Kalina admits that it could affect grain crops, which would affect prices in several months.
PRAVO - According to the Transport and Communications Ministry, damages to northern Moravian roads and railways caused by the floods come to about three billion crowns.

- According to the Czech representative Petr Palecka, some member countries of the WTO agreed in Geneva that introducing an import deposit system in the Czech Republic is not in accordance with regulations for protecting the country's balance of payments.

- A new business plan from the administrative council of Czech Railways envisages laying off 8,700 workers by the end of this year, 6,400 next year and 2,000 people in 1999. Railway connections should decrease by 450 this year and 420 next year.
- The Czech Statistical Bureau now expects GDP growth of two percent for this year and an increase in industrial output by 2.5 percent, lower as a result of massive floods.
- Due to blocked railway tracks as a result of the foods, Nova Hut Ostrava and Trinecke Zelezarny had to restrict their production to one third of its former volume.

- Certain labour offices in the east have taken a hard line against unemployed people who do not want to help fix the damage caused by the floods. If they do not accept public jobs of this sort, they could be taken off the list at the unemployment office and they may not receive government support.

LIDOVE NOVINY - A proposal which the Regional Development Minister will present to the cabinet on Wednesday calls to lease mobile homes to resolve the situation of many families during the first few weeks after the floods.
- According to a rough estimate from the Industry and Trade Ministry, about one third of Czech industry will meet serious problems due to the floods.
-- Prague Newsroom, 420-2-24-23-0003
